text:
maria: Heads up: gcp-west4 control-plane is returning 503s for auth and /routes, provisioner failing to allocate GPU pods. Seeing 'provisioner: rate limit exceeded' in logs. Affects hosted API and Dedicated provisioning. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: New canary rollout reverted in gcp-west4 at 2141599998 (reason: API 503).

sre-oncall: @maria grabbing controlplane logs and checking kv-store health. Can you paste the provisioner errors?

maria: logs:
```
prov/allocator ERROR: rate limit exceeded allocating instance (gpu-a100) for pool 'dedicated-west4' retry=3
controlplane/api ERROR: authz fetch 503 from auth-cache key=acct:1234
```
also `curl -sS https://control.gcp-west4.redwood.internal/health` -> `{"status":"degraded","auth":"timeout","kv":"ok"}`

kevin: I see spiky egress to our region egress interface; BGP flaps observed on router sw-23 for ~30s. Might be transient network causing auth cache timeouts. Starting traffic-shift plan: 1) add fallback routing to na-west2 2) scale up burst pool (on-demand) to cover 3x provisioning requests 3) enable temporary caching TTL increase

infra-provisioner-bot: provisioner: attempted burst allocation 6/10 a100s -> quota exhausted for project-redwood-west4, request id=abcd-1234.

maria: Cost note: moving to on-demand burst will cost ~3x. If we shift traffic instead, might keep cost steady but risk higher latency for EU customers routed to NA.

kevin: Initiating traffic shift: setting routing policy to prefer na-west2 for read/write controlplane operations for non-priv customers. Command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://routing-control.redwood.internal/shift \
  -d '{"from":"gcp-west4","to":["na-west2","eu-west1"],"weight":{"na-west2":0.7,"eu-west1":0.3}}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: routing change accepted id=shift-2141600001 status=pending-propagation

sre-oncall: Monitoring: auth errors down from 40/s -> 12/s after shift; provisioner still failing to allocate new GPUs due to quota. Filing ticket to cloud ops for quota bump. @maria can you open support case?

maria: Opened: GCP support case 1234567890 — quota request and BGP flaps. Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/1234567890

kevin: Suggested short-term mitigation: enable local auth cache fallback for 60s to avoid every-request auth fetch. Patch ready:
```
# config snippet
auth.cache.enabled: true
auth.cache.ttl: 60s
auth.cache.fallback_on_error: true
```

infra-eng: Rolling patch to canary in na-west2 now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary patch deployed to na-west2 id=patch-2345 status=ok

sre-oncall: Post-shift metrics: latency p95 for generation stayed +120ms in routed regions, error budget still fine. Provisioner backlog at 18 requests. Recommend keeping shift for 3 hours, request emergency quota and then re-evaluate. :white_check_mark:

maria: Agree. We'll keep shift and avoid on-demand burst for now. Add cost tracker and tag all burst allocations to incident-2141599999.

kevin: I'll follow up with postmortem: root cause likely transient egress BGP instability causing auth cache misses and quota enforcement bubbled up as provisioner throttling. Assigning follow-ups: infra->networking to engage carrier, cloudops->quota bump, platform->auth cache resilience.

infra-provisioner-bot: provisioner: queued 18 requests, ETA for fulfillment unknown.

maria: Thanks all — sending incident notification to ops@ and paging product for impacted customers.
